incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired PD-63782 -> inference-eu: increased 5xx rate on embedding-queue (region: eu-central). Auto-escalation to oncall in 30s. Links: https://pagerduty.redwood/pd/PD-63782 :rotating_light:
PagerDuty Bot: Alert details: 503/504 spike, customer error surface reported by customer-id: CUST-982, approx 18% request error rate over last 3m. Impact: degraded embeddings for EU tenants (best-effort fallback in us-west in flow).
sam: ack — grabbing the bridge. I'm oncall for infra today.
alex: ack, joining. first pass: checking autoscaler, request queue depth, and KV cache error logs.
maria: ping — support getting chatter from two paying EU customers, want ETA for a public note.
sam: quick status: scaling looks normal, but k8s nodes show elevated pod restarts on embedder-v2. logs -> `embedder_v2: upstream read timeout` repeated.
alex: pulling pod logs now. tail: ```
2026-03-15T19:03:11Z embedder_v2 error: upstream read timeout
2026-03-15T19:03:12Z embedder_v2 warn: retrying request (attempt 2)
2026-03-15T19:03:13Z cache_kv ERROR get shard-17 timeout after 1500ms
```
sam: interesting — cache_kv timeouts. Could be network flap to the KV cluster in eu-central. Can someone run a quick tcpdump on one of the failing nodes?
alex: running `kubectl exec -it embedder-v2-58b -- bash -c "tcpdump -nni eth0 port 11211 or port 11212 -c 200" > /tmp/tcpdump.pcap` now.
kevin: joining the bridge. I've looked at metric spikes earlier — net dev drops on node eu-node-7 around 18:56 UTC. Might be hardware NIC issues.
maria: customer note draft: "We're investigating elevated errors for embedding generation in EU regions. We're working on mitigation and will update in 15 minutes." ok to send?
sam: hold — confirm rollback/mitigation first. If we can failover traffic to us-west for affected customers temporarily that's safer. alex, how long to flip routing for the customer list?
alex: routing control uses feature-flagged route policy. I can flip a per-customer route in ~3-5 minutes for small lists. If we do global failover that's ~10 minutes plus cache warm-up.
PagerDuty Bot: acknowledged by sam at 19:04:12 UTC. PagerDuty escalation paused.
k evin: (typo) kevin: pushing to taint eu-node-7 to drain to avoid further restarts: `kubectl taint nodes eu-node-7 node.kubernetes.io/unavailable:NoSchedule-` then drain. Doing now.
sam: coordination — alex, please prepare route-update for top 5 paying EU customers (CUST-982, CUST-661, CUST-711, CUST-234, CUST-090). We'll do staged failover.
alex: preparing patch now. snippet: ```json
{"match": ["CUST-982","CUST-661"], "route_override": "us-west-embedder"}
```
kevin: node drain completed on eu-node-7. Observed immediate drop in pod restarts. Network errors trending down on that host.
alex: pushed route override for CUST-982 and CUST-661. Monitoring.
(5m later)
sam: status ping — error rate for those two customers dropped from ~18% to ~2%. Good. Continuing staged flips for the rest.
maria: sending customer note update now: "We've mitigated the primary source of errors for affected customers by routing requests to an alternate region. We're monitoring to restore normal routing once healthy; next update in 15 minutes." :email:
PagerDuty Bot: PD-63782 -> note added by sam: "staged failover to us-west for key customers; draining suspected eu-node-7."
alex: follow-up — cache_kv shard-17 still showing occasional 500s but overall throughput healthy. Setting alert suppression for PD noise.
sam: agreed, suppress auto-repages once steady for 10m.
kevin: I'll open a hardware ticket for eu-node-7 NIC and schedule repair/replace.
maria: closing loop with customers: they acknowledged, asked for root cause once known.
sam: handoff — I'm staying until we see 30m of stable errors <1% globally. After that I'll hand back to next rotation. kevin, you own the hardware ticket and root cause. alex, keep an eye on cache shard recovery. maria, keep customer comms.
alex: copy. will post logs and a small postmortem draft once RCA starts.
kevin: copy, will add hardware ticket link to the thread when created.
incident-bot: Bridge closed by sam at 19:36:40 UTC, incident remains monitored.```
